a: GET, PUT, DELETE should be idempotent; POST usually is not.
Retry-After tells clients how long to wait before retrying.
Exponential backoff increases wait time between retries (often with jitter).
HTTP keep-alive reuses TCP connections to reduce handshake overhead.
Clients send Accept-Encoding: gzip/br; servers may compress responses.
User-Agent identifies the client; some APIs require a clear UA string.
Clients and servers agree on representation via Accept and Content-Type.
Large uploads can use multipart forms or resumable chunked upload APIs.
WebSockets stay open for bidirectional messages; HTTP is request/response.
SSE streams server→client events over HTTP.
gRPC is efficient binary RPC; REST is ubiquitous HTTP+JSON for public APIs.
DNS TTL controls how long resolvers cache a DNS answer.
